    Remove a value from a comma-separated string if present

    remove_value_if_present.Rd

    Used for select-multiple survey questions where a value should be removed from a comma-separated response string — either because it duplicates a paired single-select field (e.g. a "primary" activity also listed in an "additional activities" field), or because a manually specified value (e.g. "None") should be dropped when other items were also selected, due to validation limitations in the original survey instrument.

    remove_value_if_present(
  list_col,
  remove_val,
  empty_value = "888",
  if_empty = c("replace", "keep_original")
)

    Arguments

    list_col

    Character vector of comma-separated values, one string per row.

    remove_val

    Character vector of values to remove. Either length 1 (applied to every row, e.g. "None") or the same length as list_col (one value per row, e.g. a paired activity_primary column).

    empty_value

    Character. The value to return if removing remove_val leaves nothing behind, and if_empty = "replace". This is normally an invalidation code (default is "888"), not an actual response value.

    if_empty

    Character. Controls what happens when removing remove_val leaves no items behind.

    • "replace" (default): return empty_value. Use this when an empty result means the response is invalid — e.g. the only additional activity selected duplicated the primary activity.

    • "keep_original": return list_col unchanged. Use this when remove_val by itself is a valid, meaningful answer — e.g. a respondent who only selected "None".

    Value

    A character vector the same length as list_col. Rows where list_col or the corresponding remove_val is NA are returned unchanged (NA).

    Examples

    # Row-varying value to remove (e.g. primary duplicated in additional list)
remove_value_if_present(c("A,B,C", "A,B"), c("B", "A"))
#> [1] "A,C" "B"  
#> c("A,C", "B")

# Constant value to remove, invalid if nothing left
remove_value_if_present(c("None,A", "B,C"), "None")
#> [1] "A"   "B,C"
#> c("A", "B,C")

# Constant value to remove, but "None" alone is a valid response
remove_value_if_present(c("None,A", "None"), "None", if_empty = "keep_original")
#> [1] "A"    "None"
#> c("A", "None")
